nodes.name: Lumber Camp
nodes.offers: Build a Lumber Camp, hire a Lumberer, and get the Work Scepter.
details: Lumber Camp plan + Lumberer emblem (1 Coin, 2 flint)
Work Scepter recipe for marking work areas
nodes.flavor: First the axe, then everything else.

nodes.name: Builder's Hut
nodes.offers: Hire a Builder: they fill the gaps on any building's checklist, build blueprints for you, and lay barricade lines.
details: Builder's Hut plan + Builder emblem (moved off the Lumber Camp; old worlds that owned the Lumber Camp keep them)
Upgrade Orders (hut level 2): on any plaque that says 'next level: add X', order the Builder to add the missing pieces from your stores (beds, lights, labels, a planked floor...)
Blueprints for every building whose plan you know; levels and home tiers still come only from the plaque checklist
Barricade lines: a first-raid village can rush barricades without Defense Plans
Stone floors in Upgrade Orders need Masonry
nodes.flavor: Tell me what the room is missing, and I will fetch my hammer.

nodes.name: Sharpened Axes
nodes.offers: Lumberers fell each tree 10% faster, and every 8 trees they whet the axe at the camp grindstone.
details: Existing: felling time -10%
New: every 8 trees, the Lumberer whets his axe at the Lumber Camp grindstone (sparks and sound); a camp without one, he whets on the spot
nodes.flavor: A keen edge is half the day's work.

nodes.name: Fisher's Nets
nodes.offers: Casts finish 10% sooner, and the Fisher keeps a net in the water: 1 fish an hour, up to 4.
details: Existing: cast cycle -10%
New: the Fisher sets a net in the water (a visible buoy); it holds 1 fish per in-game hour, up to 4, which he hauls in at the start of work and whenever it is full
nodes.flavor: Mend the net, and the net feeds you while you sleep.

nodes.name: Sawmill & Sawyer
nodes.offers: A Sawyer turns logs into planks and Timber Beams.
details: Sawmill plan + Sawyer emblem
Seasoned Timber research: sawing -15% time
Timber Beams feed the Coster's Cart, Deep Mine and Guild Halls
nodes.flavor: The saw sings; the village grows.

nodes.name: Mill, Bakery & Pasture
nodes.offers: Millers, Bakers, Herders and Butchers: bread in bulk, wool, leather and meat.
details: Mill, Bakery, Pasture and Butcher plans + Miller, Baker, Herder and Butcher emblems (2 Coins + goods each)
Flour -> bread in bulk frees the Innkeeper and fills the meal reserve
Wool feeds beds and Wool Bolts; hides feed the Tannery
Better Yeast research: baking -15%
nodes.flavor: Grind, knead, shear: the steady heartbeat of a village.
depends_on: Emblem entries + release GameTests for 4 trades

nodes.name: Hunters' Lodge
nodes.offers: A Hunter ranges beyond the walls and brings back meat, feathers and hides.
details: Hunters' Lodge plan + Hunter emblem (2 Coins, 4 flint, 8 sticks)
Carcasses are butchered at the lodge table into meat, feathers and hides
Hides feed the Tannery: leather comes from hunting, not before it
nodes.flavor: The forest gives, if you know where to look.

nodes.gate_text: Own the Hunters' Lodge or Mill, Bakery & Pasture (a hide source)
nodes.name: Tannery & Tanner
nodes.offers: A Tanner cures hides into leather and Cured Hide.
details: Tannery plan + Tanner emblem (moved off Mine, Smelter & Smithy; old worlds that owned it keep them)
Cured Hide feeds the Porters' Guild and Armoury gear: the tanner -> leather -> packs chain
Tanning Acid research (-15% time) can now be started

nodes.name: Mine, Smelter & Smithy
nodes.offers: Mine ore, smelt iron and forge tools. Lumberers and Miners holding an iron tool work 10% faster (diamond or netherite: 20%).
details: Mine, Smelter and Smithy plans + Miner, Smelter and Smith emblems
Smith makes iron tools and swords for equipment requests
Tool tiers: a Lumberer or Miner holding an iron tool fells and cuts 10% faster; diamond or netherite 20%
Blast Bellows research (smelting -15%) can now be started
Gear: opens Gear Tier 2 (Plate: iron armour, crossbows) for Veteran guards, Sharpshooters and level-5 workers; any one of Iron Arms Drill, Armoury or Mine, Smelter & Smithy counts
Tannery moved to its own node; Carpenter, Mason and Weaver moved to Carpenter, Mason & Weaver
nodes.flavor: Stone to ore, ore to bloom, bloom to blade.

nodes.name: Carpenter, Mason & Weaver
nodes.offers: Workshops for furniture, stone bricks and Wool Bolts, the stuff towns are built from.
details: Carpenter, Mason and Weaver plans + emblems (moved off Mine, Smelter & Smithy; old worlds that owned it keep them)
Masons cut stone bricks for walls, houses and charters
Weavers turn wool into Wool Bolts for beds, banners and the Crown
nodes.flavor: Measure twice, cut once, and the town stands a hundred years.

nodes.name: Charcoal Kilns
nodes.offers: Every Smelter batch takes 25% less time and 25% less effort, so a Smelter finishes more ingots and charcoal a day.
details: Smelter batches (iron, copper, gold, bloom, charcoal): -25% time and -25% effort
Stacks with Blast Bellows research
Pick one: Kilns or Deep Mine
nodes.flavor: Smoke all night, iron all day.

nodes.name: Deep Mine
nodes.offers: The Miner digs his shaft down to a second level, where the rock face gives more iron and gold, plus redstone, lapis and rare diamonds. 15% of the ore he finds gives 1 extra ore.
details: A second mine level 16 blocks below the first (an old quarry mine digs 12 -> 14 deep)
15% of mined ore blocks yield +1 ore
Pick one: Kilns or Deep Mine
nodes.flavor: Deeper, lads. The good stuff is always deeper.

nodes.name: Masters & Apprentices
nodes.offers: Workers who share a workshop with a master (trade level 5+) earn 50% more trade XP.
details: Any worker whose workplace also employs a settler at trade level 5+ earns +50% trade XP per finished job
Works in every workplace with two or more worker slots (Smithy, Bakery, Mason, Lumber Camp, Mine...)
A master beside another master learns faster too
nodes.flavor: Watch my hands, not my face.

nodes.name: Guild Halls
nodes.offers: Crafted goods roll their quality as if the crafter were 2 trade levels higher: Fine or better far more often.
details: Every workshop's quality roll counts the crafter as 2 trade levels higher
Example: a level-3 crafter in a level-1 workshop makes Fine or better about 80% of the time instead of about 45%
Masterwork still needs a real trade level 7, Legendary a real level 9
Better grades sell for more (merchant purse still caps each visit)
nodes.flavor: Every master has a hall; every hall has a feast day.
